{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABc6sthA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhGc2bs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 22, "title": "Make direct body-part manipulation drive MotionBricks-generated reactions in the rest of the body", "body": "## Product intent — direct manipulation drives *generated reactions* in the rest of the body

**This is the clarified user requirement, superseding the interpretation that a specific "Push / Balance" interaction was the desired feature.**

> A person clicks/grabs **any suitable body part** (hand, foot, head, torso, pelvis, etc.) on a standing SOMA or MMD avatar and moves or rotates it freely with the mouse. **MotionBricks should generate as much of the rest of the body's animation as possible in response to that externally imposed motion**, with the manipulated part following the human's input. The character should feel alive and reactive, not like a pose editor or a rigid model being translated. Stumbling, counterbalance or stepping are **possible emergent examples**, not required modes or preauthored actions.

The **point is interaction-conditioned whole-body motion generation**, not push forces, dedicated push buttons, a scripted balance controller, or simply animating a full-body pose authored by IK.

### Why the implemented demos are not the acceptance target

- [#17 / PR #18](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/pull/18) implemented useful Move/Rotate pose editing and opt-in ONNX playback. In `src/pose-ik.ts`, `Hips` selection assigns `pose.root = target`, moving the entire avatar. `src/pose-response.ts` creates full-body goals by blending to an **IK-completed pose**, so manipulation can be mostly predetermined and the model is used to transition between prescribed poses. Post-generation IK may also overwrite the generated effect.
- [#19 / PRs #20 and #21](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/issues/19) implemented a **separate Push / Balance mode** with measured real ONNX recovery cases. That work is valid *for the narrower balance use case*, but the user explicitly says **this is not what they asked for**. Do not require choosing Push mode or define success as a "stumble". The historical completed issues and PRs should remain intact.
- The original keyboard locomotion, MMD Toon/outline/physics, and asset handling must not regress.

## User-facing interaction

1. In the **main interactive pose studio workflow**, let the user directly hold and continuously move/rotate one body part while the character visibly responds elsewhere. This should be the primary interaction, **not** an additional purpose-built Push mode. Controls can remain Move/Rotate or be clarified/reorganized, but don't route all generated responses through the specialized BalanceRecovery policy.
2. A held hand should follow the cursor to a feasible extent, while the other arm, shoulders, torso, pelvis, legs, and root can respond based on **actual MotionBricks output**. Likewise for a foot, head/chest or pelvis interaction. The character's whole body must not translate rigidly with the grabbed pelvis/hips unless that is an actual coherent generated response.
3. Continue response generation **during a sustained drag** and through release; respond to trajectory, velocity and changing targets, not only an endpoint or preauthored event. Provide a natural settling response on release without forcing a particular stock pose or mandatory step.
4. Without loaded WebGPU/ONNX, keep a clearly labeled IK-only preview, but do **not** present it as the intended AI reaction. Prevent camera/pointer conflicts and handle low inference frame rate smoothly.

## Engineering plan / feasibility requirements

**A. Separate controlled DOFs from generated DOFs.** Track the **selected part's world-space position/orientation, target trajectory and control state**, versus the rest of the body. Apply deterministic manipulation only as minimally needed for responsiveness, joint reach and skin coherence. Avoid solving a complete authored "correct" target pose and then prescribing all its joints to the model. Keep a clear boundary between hard human input, minimal kinematic constraints and model-controlled joints.

**B. Investigate the real ONNX conditioning contract.** Current `src/motion.ts` `encode(context, targets, rig)` uses four historical **full-body** poses and four target **full-body** poses; its presence masks are per-frame tensors rather than an obvious arbitrary per-joint mouse-control channel. **Do not claim partial-joint hard constraints are natively supported.** Inspect actual model input semantics, masks, conditioning influence and documented limitations. Design the best feasible conditioning from the observed manipulated-joint trajectory, recency/velocity and current plausible pose, while leaving other-joint goals as neutral/non-prescriptive as the interface allows. Explore control timing/weights and, if supported, legitimate masking techniques; do not invent unsupported mask semantics. Report how much raw ONNX output genuinely depends on a moving control versus a static IK-completed target.

**C. Generate and blend the rest of the body.** Maintain a continuous 30 Hz recent-pose/target context, schedule/coalesce pointer changes without invalidating *every* useful response, and safely blend new ONNX segments while the pointer moves. Correct the *directly manipulated part* with bounded constrained IK to match the human's input; preserve the generated motion of unrelated joints as much as possible. Do not override the entire generated body with a full-body deterministic solver on every frame. Track the cause of all motion (pointer, IK, ONNX, contact/physics).

**D. Motion quality and contacts.** Keep a plausible skeleton and bounded joint rotations; support feet/contact stabilization as a **limited, transparent constraint**, not as a scripted reaction. If the model spontaneously yields counterbalance, weight shift, extra steps or similar behavior, allow it; do not hardcode those as universal requirements. For grabbing hips/pelvis, distinguish changing the selected root constraint from translating the whole character or pretending the body independently responded.

**E. SOMA + MMD.** Use canonical SOMA pose space for ONNX and the existing retargeting for Animasa Miku and Uka. Preserve Toon, outlines and secondary physics, and avoid physics fighting the manipulated portion. Ensure fresh model switching, reset, pointer cancel, model-load failures and resource cleanup remain reliable.

**F. Feasibility evidence and fallback.** The pretrained MotionBricks checkpoint may not be able to condition on arbitrary partial-body interaction at sufficient quality. Run **real ONNX A/B tests** before asserting success. If it cannot produce visibly meaningful movement of *uncontrolled* joints under this conditioning contract, report that as a limitation; propose a compatible controller, a different model or training as a **separate** next step. Do not substitute hand-authored movement and label it AI-generated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default/primary mouse manipulation flow (not Push mode) supports grabbing/moving/rotating useful body parts with immediate feedback and **continuous real MotionBricks responses elsewhere** when ONNX is enabled; generated motion can continue while still dragging and after release.
- [ ] Demonstrations include at least **hand manipulation and pelvis/torso manipulation**: the manipulated point follows the user; the rest of the character is *not* rigidly translated or frozen and is not entirely determined by authored IK; any balancing/stepping is an observed response, not an imposed animation.
- [ ] Measure and show **per-joint displacement/rotation caused by raw decoded ONNX versus minimal direct IK** for non-manipulated joints. Record full input condition windows, raw vs displayed trajectories, control joint errors, generated joint changes, root motion and timing. At least two distinct drag trajectories must have distinct substantive model outputs; compare against no-drag and IK-only baselines.
- [ ] Verify that post-generation corrections are restricted/bounded, with quantitative evidence they are **not responsible for the claimed natural response**. Separate MotionBricks motion from retargeting, contact support and secondary MMD physics.
- [ ] Smooth motion with held/cancelled/reversed drag, release, stale in-flight inference and latency; no snap-back, large teleport, invalid joint deformation or runaway queues.
- [ ] SOMA, Animasa Miku and Uka share controls and observable model-driven reactions. Existing pose-editing behavior, specialist Push / Balance mode and keyboard locomotion remain functional; no unrelated new modes required.
- [ ] Unit tests for controlled-versus-generated joint ownership, context creation and mask semantics, motion stitching and cancellation; browser checks with actual pointer drags and real ONNX WebGPU inference. Pages build/tests/deployment pass, docs accurately distinguish feasibility and measured success.

### Implementation orientation

Prioritize proving **one believable continuous interaction** (e.g. grab/drag a hand and observe model-generated motion in other joints) end-to-end, then generalize to foot, head and pelvis. If the model cannot do it with available conditioning, document that plainly and keep the Issue open until a viable approach is agreed and implemented.

Relevant files: `src/pose-main.ts`, `src/pose-pointer.ts`, `src/pose-response.ts`, `src/pose-ik.ts`, `src/motion.ts`, `src/balance.ts`, `src/mmd.ts`, `docs/pose-validation.md`, `docs/balance-merged-validation.md`.
